messages:
Lucas (eng-platform): Noticed weird chart on the latency dashboard for endpoint /v1/generate — p95 jumped ~300ms in the last 10m but p50 and p99 are flat. Screenshot: https://console.redwood.internal/d/latency/789 :thinking_face:
Nina (telemetry): flat p99 with p95 spike suggests a sampling or interpolation artifact. Do we have spiky mid-tail chunking on that route?
Omar (backend): We recently changed the rollout routing for that endpoint to send 20% traffic to a new variant with a slightly different batching strategy. Could be interaction with how we aggregate across variants.
Sofia (console): The dashboard uses histogram interpolation when sample counts are low, otherwise it uses tdigest-derived quantiles. Which path is active for this timeframe?
Lucas (eng-platform): Querying raw counts now. Quick SQL: 
```
SELECT route, ts_bucket, histogram_buckets, tdigest_size
FROM route_latency_agg
WHERE route = '/v1/generate' AND ts >= now() - interval '15 minutes'
ORDER BY ts_bucket DESC
```
Sofia (console): If histogram_buckets exists the UI prefers the histogram-based pctl_estimate. If we merged sketches from variants inconsistently we can get mid-quantile wobble.
Nina (telemetry): Also check if quota-fallbacks happened. When a client hits quota we route to the pooled fallback which has different latency distribution; mixing a small number of fallback samples can move p95 significantly but leave p99 unchanged if fallback sits between p50 and p95.
Omar (backend): Good call. I see a handful of 429->fallback flows in the logs around ts 1749499980. The fallback pool has median ~60ms but heavier mass at ~220ms which could raise p95.
Lucas (eng-platform): So possible hypothesis: small number of fallback samples + histogram interpolation led to p95 bump. How do we prevent customers from misreading this as regression?
Sofia (console): We should show sample_count per-quantile in the tooltip and surface an "aggregation-mode" pill (histogram vs sketch vs raw) in the top-left. Also a subtle warning badge when sample_count < 500 in the window.
Nina (telemetry): Telemetry suggestion: emit a tag when a timeseries switches aggregation-mode during a single chart window (e.g., histogram->tdigest). That would let us alert on mixed-aggregation artifacts.
Omar (backend): Longer term we should unify aggregation at storage level: prefer server-side rehydrated raw samples for final pctl calculation when available, fall back to deterministic histogram interpolation otherwise. Also make sure variant routing tags are preserved so we can breakdown by variant.
Lucas (eng-platform): For immediate mitigation: can we add on-UI a small legend note: "p95 may be sensitive to low sample counts and fallback routes" and a link to docs about how fallbacks and routing affect percentiles?
Sofia (console): Yep, I can add the pill + tooltip in a tiny patch. Will also make the tooltip include the per-quantile sample_count.
Nina (telemetry): I'll add the telemetry event for aggregation-mode-change and a rule to surface an internal alert when mixed-mode and sample_count < 1000.
Omar (backend): I'll add route-tag preservation in the ingest path and a small fix to ensure fallback events are annotated with "route_variant=fallback" before sketches are emitted.
ci-bot: ci build succeeded for sofi/quantile-pills PR #4082 — staging deploy scheduled. :white_check_mark:
Lucas (eng-platform): Nice. After staging deploy let's re-evaluate same time window, and run a synthetic where we inject 200 fallback events to see p95 sensitivity.
Sofia (console): Will watch. I'll also add the aggregation-mode badge only for the new charts first so we have time to tweak wording.
Nina (telemetry): Quick experiment result: simulated 200 fallback samples moved p95 by ~280ms in the 10m window at n~3k total. I'll post the notebook and graphs in the thread shortly. :bar_chart:
Lucas (eng-platform): Thanks everyone. Once we confirm in staging, let's add a short note in the changelog and the incident playbook about interpreting percentile spikes when fallback routing/aggregation flips happen.
Omar (backend): Agreed. Adding a tiny telemetry flag to mark rollouts that activate fallback routes so we can correlate automatically.
Sofia (console): PR merged to staging, monitoring the deploy now. :eyes:
